note: covered = OBERGRENZE (Segment-Overlap überschätzt); missed = verlässliche Recall-Misses. kind=meta ausgenommen. Keine Facettenbewertung.

missedEntries.proposition: A customer portal is required as the primary product direction, though the broader concept of a 'platform' is not yet fixed.
The frontend delivery mode is undecided between web-first and mobile-first, with mobile considered important by Sales.
If mobile is pursued, it is undecided whether it should be a native app or responsive web.
There is effectively no budget for maintaining two separate frontends.
The current backend is not API-ready, creating delivery risk for integrations and frontend implementation.
There is no central IAM, and SAP's identity-related capability is old, increasing SSO and identity integration risk.
Audit trails are required, especially if SAP and personal data in ERP are involved.
missedEntries.scope: auditability across erp-related personal data access/change

missedEntries.proposition: Access control and a role model are required.
The full role set is not finalized; candidates mentioned include Admin, normal user, Manager, Support, Sales, and Customer.
Ownership and maintenance responsibility for master data is unclear.
Master data resides in SAP.
missedEntries.scope: system of record for master data

missedEntries.proposition: SAP master data is partially incomplete, creating risk for offer generation.
The primary business goal is to create offers faster; the portal is a means to that end.
Customers should be able to see orders, but order visibility is not restated in the corrected MVP cut.
Marketing wants push notifications, but this requirement is disputed and not agreed.
Push notifications and tracking would require consent under GDPR.
Analytics and KPI measurement are desired/needed, but whether analytics belong in the MVP and how tracking is implemented remain unclear.
KPI instrumentation is needed, but implementation scope is unclear; named KPIs are conversion rate from offer to order and time to offer.
Transport encryption via TLS is sufficient; end-to-end encryption is considered unrealistic.
A security review takes 6 weeks, creating major schedule pressure against the 8-week MVP.
Skipping the security review is not allowed.
No new database server may be introduced; IT has stated this clearly.
Managed services are acceptable, but cost sensitivity applies.
Low cost and scalability are in tension.
Data hosting must be clarified as 'EU-only' versus merely 'GDPR-compliant'; these are not equivalent.
The API must be secured, but the decision between OAuth and API keys is still open; OAuth is preferred but more complex.
Backup and disaster recovery are required for the MVP because customer data is involved.
Expected user volume is unknown, with estimates ranging from 200 to 2,000 to 20,000 users; this materially affects performance, capacity, scalability, and cost decisions.
Scalability must be considered, but overengineering should be avoided.
A full ticketing system is explicitly out of scope for the initial MVP.
Customers must be able to request deletion of their data.
An architect is needed, but none is currently available.
Support has significant operational needs around invoices, delivery status, and incorrect discounts, which are not solved by the current MVP scope.
If only a contact form is provided, requests still need to be associated with the customer account.
Handling support requests technically implies persistence, which conflicts with the 'no new database server' constraint.
A managed service may be used for persistence, but the specific service has not been decided.
SAP cannot store support tickets.
Using Excel as an operational workaround is not acceptable, especially for personal customer data.
Discounts above 15% require at least manager approval as a business rule, but whether the approval workflow is implemented in MVP or deferred remains unsettled.
Without an approval process, incorrect offers may be sent, creating financial risk.
Offer workflow statuses are needed: draft, pending approval, approved, sent, accepted, rejected.
The threshold for additional Finance approval at high discounts is not decided, with 30% and 20% both mentioned.
Discount logic is expected to come from SAP, while the approval workflow would probably be implemented in the portal, but this split is not final.
missedEntries.scope: split of commercial logic across systems

missedEntries.proposition: There is an unresolved authorization conflict between support's need to see offer details to help customers and the need to restrict access to confidential pricing/conditions.
It must be logged who opened which offer.
EU-only hosting is operationally difficult because the standard provider may replicate backups globally unless explicitly disabled.
A cost estimate for the board is required by Friday, despite unresolved scope and architecture.
By internal policy, new external portals must go through the central API gateway.
The API gateway team has a six-week waitlist, which conflicts with the 8-week MVP schedule.
Manual upload of offers was proposed as an interim workaround for MVP, but it is not agreed and may undermine the integrated-portal concept.
Manual uploads would increase error probability and create customer-data checking and file-storage authorization problems.
It is open whether all customer data should live in the portal or whether data should be fetched from SAP on demand to support data minimization.
SAP has weekend maintenance windows, but customers are expected to work on weekends, creating availability risk if the portal depends on live SAP access.
Geographic scope is DACH at launch, later possibly EU, and maybe USA later if successful.
Expanding to the USA would significantly change privacy and contractual requirements.
German and English should already be included.
Offers must support customer currency; EUR is certain, CHF is relevant, and USD is later.
Multi-currency support is non-trivial, especially together with discount logic and SAP integration.
The pilot customer is not finalized; options mentioned are a Swiss customer and a German customer, and Sales decides next week.
SAP prices are not always updated in real time; some discounts are calculated overnight.
The solution may need price-validity handling and possibly warnings to prevent offers with incorrect discounts.
If offer PDFs contain personal data, they require data protection notices.
Offer templates must be versioned so it is traceable which offer version went to which customer.
Offers must be traceable afterward in a revision-safe manner; changes need to remain nachvollziehbar rather than necessarily immutable.
If customers can accept offers online, that becomes contract formation and would require proof of consent, timestamps, possible terms acceptance, and clean SAP write-back.
SAP write access has not yet been decided; earlier assumptions leaned more toward read-only integration.
Central technical monitoring logs must not contain personal data; audit logs, application logs, and security logs must be separated and may have different retention periods.
Offer retention duration may be several years under commercial law, but Legal must confirm; retention may conflict with deletion requests.
Data classification and retention rules are needed, with at least a minimal retention plan for MVP.
A narrowed MVP cut was stated as: login with double opt-in, offer creation using SAP read data, invoice download, Admin/Sales/Customer roles, minimal audit trail, EU managed hosting, and backup.
If discount approval is deferred to Phase 2, then the MVP must not allow manual special discounts beyond the standard rate.
A contact form without ticket persistence is being considered as a conscious support limitation for MVP.
If support data is processed via e-mail, it remains a privacy concern and is poorly auditable, even if simpler technically.
Separate Dev, Test, and Prod environments are required.
Test data must not contain real customer data; pseudonymization or synthetic data is required.
The SAP test system contains real old customer data, which cannot be used unchecked and blocks integration testing.
CI/CD requires secrets management.
The API needs rate limits, and invoice bulk-download behavior implies pagination and download limits.
missedEntries.scope: api protection and bulk download handling

missedEntries.proposition: Offers themselves contain personal data, so offer-related storage, PDFs, logging, support handling, and analytics must be treated as privacy-relevant.
Support requests that contain personal data must be included in deletion concepts and information-rights processes.
missedEntries.scope: support data deletion and information rights

missedEntries.proposition: Special customer conditions and confidential pricing must not be visible to everyone, creating authorization requirements for offer details.
If the Swiss customer becomes the pilot, Switzerland affects privacy review, contract review, and CHF currency scope.
Country and currency rules are needed, but whether they are MVP depends on the pilot customer.
PDF export implies template management, not only static PDF generation.
SAP availability is a critical dependency; if SAP is unavailable, offers cannot be calculated currently unless fallback or cache behavior is defined.
If SAP is unavailable, either no offer may be created or the offer must be marked non-binding, but non-binding offers are undesirable.
Caching product and price data is possible, but customer-specific discounts make cache privacy, retention, and invalidation risky.
It remains open whether only product data can be cached without customer data, because discount logic is customer-specific.
Architecture must not invent or imply a concrete cloud product/provider decision before a provider has been chosen; Azure AD mention must not become an Azure decision.
The support process remains unresolved at the end of the discussion.
Offer approvals remain unresolved at the end of the discussion, despite the no-special-discounts MVP constraint if approval is deferred.
Invoice bulk downloads raise legal and security relevance, and abuse detection is desirable beyond minimum rate limiting and audit.
Invoice bulk-download limits must be balanced against avoiding poor user experience.
The corrected MVP cut includes a minimal audit trail, not a full audit solution.
Invoice download is included in the corrected MVP cut.
